knowledge:
- key_parameters: averror=The maximum acceptable information loss or average error allowed when defining regions (e.g., 0.01 for 1% error)
- alternatives: CGHcall=Used to perform the initial segmentation and calling of copy number states before running CGHregions
- when_to_use: Use when you have multi-sample array CGH data that has already been segmented and called, and you need to simplify the dataset into discrete regions of gain, loss, or normality for downstream analysis.
- pitfalls: Attempting to run CGHregions directly on raw log2-ratios or unsegmented data will fail; the input must be a called CGH object (such as a cghCall object).

workflows.name: cgh_dimension_reduction
workflows.intent: Reduce segmented and called array CGH data into genomic regions of minimal information loss and visualize the results.
input: called_cgh_data.RData (an object of class cghCall containing segmented and called array CGH data)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and input data ;; 2. Run the CGHregions dimension reduction algorithm ;; 3. Inspect and plot the resulting genomic regions
workflows.code:
library(CGHregions)
data(WiltingCalled)
WiltingCalled
regions <- CGHregions(WiltingCalled, averror=0.01)
regions
plot(regions)
